uncited: Joint Pose and Radiance Field Optimization solves the problem of reconstructing a 3D scene from an unposed image collection by simultaneously optimizing the neural radiance field parameters and the camera extrinsic (and optionally intrinsic) parameters.

It distinguishes itself from methods that assume known poses by treating camera poses as learnable variables in the optimization loop, thereby addressing the "chicken-and-egg" problem where pose estimation requires a good scene model and vice versa.

This approach builds on [Camera Pose and Extrinsic/Intrinsic Optimization](12051-camera-pose-and-extrinsic-intrinsic-optimization.md) by extending the optimization domain to include the scene representation itself.
The problem of optimizing camera poses alongside radiance fields emerged as a solution to the dependency on Structure-from-Motion (SfM) pipelines, which can fail on textureless or repetitive scenes.
These methods laid the groundwork for more complex joint optimization strategies like RoDynRF, VMRF, and NeRF Pose and Appearance Optimization.
